conviction.explanation: At 48x trailing earnings, observed EPS decline despite higher group profit and externally funded capital-intensive expansion create unfavorable current purchase compensation. Backlog and better margins prevent a strong sell; unavailable June cash/debt further limits confidence without being the sole bearish reason.

executive_summary:
Solarvest’s project opportunity is credible: Q1 revenue grew 13.2%, profit 19.8% and margin improved to 12.2%, with RM2.371bn orderbook. Historical FY26 CFO turned positive and simple FCF was RM32.112m before expansion investments.

The entry proposition is weaker than the group-growth headline: basic EPS fell from 2.11 to 1.99sen at 48x trailing earnings, and FY26 equity-related proceeds were RM386.821m. Investment-property and associate/JV outlays exceeded the simple surplus. A modest sell view reflects delivered dilution and premium exposure; March balances cannot establish current June funding.
bull_case: Profitable order conversion could eventually outgrow dilution and turn improving project margins into per-share cash gains.
bear_case: Dilution, capital demands and collections may keep owner returns behind profit growth while the premium contracts.
key_uncertainties: Current June 30 full balance-sheet/cash-flow attachment unavailable; March evidence is older.
Cash after expansion outlays beyond simple PP&E/intangible FCF.
catalysts_upcoming: Comparable Q1 EPS above the prior 2.11sen with maintained margins would challenge the per-share objection.
Current statements showing positive cash after all specified expansion outlays would reduce funding concerns.

correlation_notes: Low beta (0.55) — historically less sensitive to broad-market moves.
Sector: Technology — use sector-specific catalysts and risks in the thesis.
risk_assessment.max_drawdown_scenario: Historical max drawdown: 71.1% over available price history. Projected worst case (2-sigma): ~89.7% from current $4.37.

action_plan.note: Signal too mixed for precise levels (conviction +0.00, convergence 0.18). Wait for a clearer setup.

research_verdict.thesis: Solarvest shows improving project profitability but has not delivered per-share growth: Q1 EPS fell to 1.99 sen from 2.11 despite higher profit. The bear carries that distinction at 48x trailing earnings, with expansion outlays exceeding the dated simple FCF bridge. A verified RM2.371bn backlog and margin improvement preserve future conversion upside, while March funding data cannot stand in for June liquidity.
research_verdict.strongest_counterexample: Q1 revenue grew 13.2%, margin improved to 12.2% from 11.5%, and FY26 CFO turned positive; profitable project delivery could eventually outgrow dilution.
invalidation_conditions: A comparable Q1 basic EPS above the prior 2.11 sen with margin at least the observed 12.2% would weaken the current per-share-growth objection.
Verified current statements showing positive cash after PP&E, intangibles, investment-property and associate/JV outlays would weaken the external-expansion-funding objection.
evidence_gaps: Latest June 30 full balance-sheet/cash-flow attachment was inaccessible; available March figures are explicitly older.
decisive_factors: Current profit growth and falling EPS are disclosed facts read differently, not a valuation-model gap.
FY26 RM386.821m equity-related funding and capital-intensive growth offset the positive orderbook.
